data.name: Alyose
data.gender_notes: Alyose is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Greek word ἀλεξίος (Alexios), meaning 'helper of the people.' In Christianity, it's associated with the name of St. Alexius, a Christian saint known for his kindness and faithfulness. The name Alyose carries the meaning “God's helper” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Alyose usually hope their child will grow to embody god's helper and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder to be a helper and a source of support in times of need.
data.etymology: Alyose belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's helper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Alyose total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.
